chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs Tawaf with the House and with As-Safa and al-Marwah, he is released from Ihram, whether he likes it or dislikes it.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim become free from Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the completion of Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i serves as the definitive act that releases the pilgrim from the restrictions of Ihram, a ruling applicable regardless of whether the pilgrer performs Qiran or Tamattu. The phrase 'whether he likes it or dislikes it' underscores the objective nature of this legal release, indicating that the pilgrim is no longer bound by Ihram prohibitions once these core rites are concluded, even if other Hajj obligations remain. This narration is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the completion of the essential pillars and the optional or supplementary acts of Hajj.
